raw_response:
I farm a small 6 mu holding, so I will keep my plan simple and steady. I have 35 years of experience, and with some family members working off-farm, I do not want a plan that depends on too much labor at one time. I also have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield when the weather turns dry. I will keep stevia as my main cash crop because that matches how I farm now, but I will still keep some wheat and maize for income balance and land use. For wheat and maize, I will use improved or hybrid seed because on a small farm I care about stable yield. For stevia, I will stay with the planting material that performs reliably for me and manage it more carefully with water and fertilizer because leaf yield is sensitive to weak growth. I will not push fertilizer too hard, because too much nitrogen can waste money and create weak plants, especially on stevia. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on my scale, easier to arrange, and fits my labor situation. I will irrigate wheat and maize a few key times, and I will irrigate stevia more often because it needs more stable moisture through the season. I will spray only as much as needed to control weeds, insects, and disease without adding unnecessary cost.
